body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.

body: ## Purpose
What happens when a Free workspace uses up its monthly included usage.
## Limits
- Free includes a fixed monthly amount of billed tokens and requests.
- Free has no overage: nothing beyond the included usage is ever charged, and Free workspaces never get an invoice.
## At the limit
Once a Free workspace reaches its monthly limit, further requests are rate-limited: the API returns HTTP `429` with error code `quota_exceeded` and a `Retry-After` header. Requests work again when the next month starts. To keep sending requests sooner, the customer upgrades to a paid plan.
_Last reviewed 2025-11-10._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/usage-credit-and-quota-guidelines-2026.json", "chunk": "4/9", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Usage Credits and Quota Assignment Guidelines for Hosted Inference (2026)", "status": "in_review", "date": "2026-02-03", "text": "Note: the matrix above is normative for assigning credits during billing cycles. Quantization and optimized kernels may reduce actual backend resource consumption; platform adjusts cost multipliers quarterly and documents changes in pricing-change-notices.
Quota types and enforcement semantics:
1) monthly_budget (hard): A monthly CR cap. When exhausted, requests receive HTTP 402 (Payment Required) with body code \"quota_exceeded.monthly_budget\" unless account configured for auto-topup.
2) concurrency (soft then hard): A per-account concurrent request cap measured over 1s windows. Soft limit issues 429 with header X-Quota-Action: slow-down and offers Retry-After. If soft limit persists for >10s, platform escalates to hard 429 with X-Quota-Blocked.
3) burst_pool (grace): Rolling 24h pool that replenishes linearly. When monthly_budget is near exhaustion, burst_pool provides allowance up to configured percentage of monthly_budget. Exhausting both results in hard-block.
Enforcement flow (simple):
1) Request arrives."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/overload-errors-and-retry-guidance.json", "chunk": "6/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API overload errors: support guidance, retry/backoff, and escalation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-12-05", "text": "(continued) ## Error payload: what customers see

}
## Canonical mapping: status → meaning → what we tell customers
Use this table to drive consistent customer guidance.
| HTTP | Typical meaning | What Support should say | Customer action |
|------|------------------|--------------------------|-----------------|
| 429 | Admission control / rate limiting / tier cap hit | “Your request was rejected to protect system stability. This is not a model failure; it indicates you are sending requests faster than the current allowed rate/concurrency.” | Respect Retry-After; implement exponential backoff + jitter; reduce concurrency; consider batching; if persistent, discuss tier/capacity options. |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/overload-errors-and-retry-guidance.json", "chunk": "13/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Hosted API overload errors: support guidance, retry/backoff, and escalation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-12-05", "text": "### “Can you increase my limits?”
Guidance:
- Confirm whether they are hitting **429** (likely limit-related) vs **503** (regional/model saturation).
- If 429 is persistent at normal traffic levels, route to CS for capacity/tier discussion.
- If 503 is persistent, treat as reliability issue and escalate to Eng.
## Known issues (Support-facing)
1) **Retry-After header missing on some overload responses**
- Symptom: Customer receives 429/503 overload payload but no Retry-After.
- Workaround: Recommend exponential backoff with jitter as above.
- Action: Escalate if reproducible; include route + correlation IDs.
2) **Fallback model not triggering as expected**
- Symptom: Customer has configured fallback but still sees repeated 503 without failover.
- Workaround: Customer can temporarily specify an alternate model/region explicitly (if acceptable) while we investigate.
- Action: Escalate; include tenant ID, configured fallback policy (what they intended), and correlation IDs.
3) **Customer interprets 503 as “platform outage”**"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/usage-accounting-retries-and-stream-cancellation.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Usage accounting: retries and streaming cancellation", "status": "published", "date": "2025-02-18", "text": "## Common customer symptoms
- We only sent N requests but we see >N rows: retries created additional attempts.
- We timed out at 15s so we expected zero bill: prompt tokens + partial completion tokens may still be counted.
## Recommended mitigations
1) Avoid automatic retries on client-side timeouts for long generations.
2) Increase client timeout where possible (align to max expected generation time).
3) Reduce max_tokens / output length to meet latency budgets.
4) For troubleshooting, ask for a small set of request_ids + the customers retry/cancel metrics."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/enterprise-priority-429-and-quota-behavior.json", "chunk": "6/16", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Enterprise priority: 429 / quota / overload behavior (Support guide)", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-06", "text": "(continued) ### A) Quota- and rate-limit-driven 429s (customer-specific)
| Category | error.type | x-redwood-429-reason (typical) | Meaning | Customer guidance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Route-group rate limit | rate_limit_exceeded | rate_limit_route_group | Customer exceeded a per-route or route-group cap. | Same as above; ask them to spread load or request a higher burst allowance. |
| Token / compute guardrail | rate_limit_exceeded | token_budget_exceeded | Customer exceeded a token/compute budget (if enabled for contract). | Reduce max_tokens / request size; smooth traffic; discuss contract sizing. |"}]}

body: ## Purpose
What happens when a Free workspace uses up its monthly included usage.
## Limits
- Free includes a fixed monthly amount of billed tokens and requests.
- Free has no overage: nothing beyond the included usage is ever charged, and Free workspaces never get an invoice.
## At the limit
Once a Free workspace reaches its monthly limit, further requests are rate-limited: the API returns HTTP `429` with error code `quota_exceeded` and a `Retry-After` header. Requests work again when the next month starts. To keep sending requests sooner, the customer upgrades to a paid plan.

Quota types and enforcement semantics:
1) monthly_budget (hard): A monthly CR cap. When exhausted, requests receive HTTP 402 (Payment Required) with body code \"quota_exceeded.monthly_budget\" unless account configured for auto-topup.
2) concurrency (soft then hard): A per-account concurrent request cap measured over 1s windows. Soft limit issues 429 with header X-Quota-Action: slow-down and offers Retry-After. If soft limit persists for >10s, platform escalates to hard 429 with X-Quota-Blocked.
3) burst_pool (grace): Rolling 24h pool that replenishes linearly. When monthly_budget is near exhaustion, burst_pool provides allowance up to configured percentage of monthly_budget. Exhausting both results in hard-block.

- We only sent N requests but we see >N rows: retries created additional attempts.
- We timed out at 15s so we expected zero bill: prompt tokens + partial completion tokens may still be counted.

body: ## Purpose
What happens when a Free workspace uses up its monthly included usage.
## Limits
- Free includes a fixed monthly amount of billed tokens and requests.
- Free has no overage: nothing beyond the included usage is ever charged, and Free workspaces never get an invoice.
## At the limit
Once a Free workspace reaches its monthly limit, further requests are rate-limited: the API returns HTTP `429` with error code `quota_exceeded` and a `Retry-After` header. Requests work again when the next month starts. To keep sending requests sooner, the customer upgrades to a paid plan.

To keep requests running past the Free-plan limit, **upgrade to a paid plan** before you reach it. Pebble AI is currently on Free and has no payment method on file, so you’ll need to choose a paid plan and set up billing. Free has no overage, so requests won’t keep running with extra usage charges.

Until the upgrade takes effect, reducing usage may help you stay within the limit. If you hit it, requests return **HTTP 429** with `quota_exceeded`; otherwise, service resumes when the next month starts.
